newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian finance minister details tax reform plans.
newsitem.headline: Italian finance minister details tax reform plans.

text.p: Italian Finance Minister Vincenzo Visco gave more details of his planned tax reform on Tuesday in a bid to defuse a growing row with opposition parties over the government's 1997 budget.
Visco said the minimum tax band would be raised to 18-20 percent from a previous 10 percent, while the maximum rate would fall to 46 percent from 51 percent.
"I hope that this proposal will be enough to re-assure people," Visco said.

Italy's opposition said on Monday it would not vote on the budget as part of a protest at government plans to take special powers which would allow it to dictate policy on key budgetary areas without having to refer back to parliament.
The most contested area concerns fiscal reform, where the finance ministry had previously provided just a bare outline of what it intended to do.
"I hope that this proposal will be enough to re-assure people," Visco said.
Parliament was suspended until 1100 GMT to give parties time to study the proposals. Parliamentary party leaders are due to meet at 1000 GMT. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
